annotation.title_clean: Does AI Have Buddha-Nature? Reflections on the Metaphysical, Soteriological, and Ethical Dimensions of Including Humanoid Robots in Religious Rituals from one Mahāyāna Buddhist Perspective
annotation.title_en: Does AI Have Buddha-Nature? Reflections on the Metaphysical, Soteriological, and Ethical Dimensions of Including Humanoid Robots in Religious Rituals from one Mahāyāna Buddhist Perspective
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 335 (Robophilosophy 2020), IOS Press
annotation.summary_en: Robophilosophy 2020 conference paper, shown here as an abstract only. It asks from a Mahāyāna Buddhist view whether humanoid robots, such as Mindar enshrined as Kannon Bodhisattva at Kōdaiji temple, can be seen as conscious, deserving of person rights, or even divine. It also considers the practical and ethical implications of "all humanoids have Buddha-nature."
key_provisions_or_claims: Temple Kōdaiji enshrined the robot Mindar as a personification of Kannon Bodhisattva.
Mahāyāna claims that insentient beings have buddha-nature may make the term 'theomorphic' inapplicable.
Explores whether humanoid robots can be conscious, deserve person rights, or be divine in a Buddhist context.
Considers the practical and ethical implications of the claim 'all humanoids have Buddha-nature'.
